A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Niso-DM and Tango-DM study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices A–G are available and readable, supporting a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on hyperplane, mesh, SO(10), and alanine-dipeptide distributions, including numerical comparisons and hyperparameter studies in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains the original numerical experiments and ablations and adds empirical SO(10) distribution comparisons in Appendix D.4, Figure 3.

M1.justification: The non-isotropic perturbation, Tango loss, rescaling, and Reverse/Annealing SDE procedures remain unchanged in Sections 4–6 and Algorithms 1–3. The new schematic illustrates these existing methods.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same hyperplane, Stanford Bunny, Spot the Cow, SO(10), and alanine-dipeptide distributions. The new trace-statistic plots concern the existing SO(10) task; correcting 'Standard Bunny' to 'Stanford Bunny' does not change coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 and 5 retain their comparator rows, including RSSM for meshes and SO(10). The added density plot compares the already evaluated Iso+res and Niso+res methods.

E3.justification: v3 adds a diagnostic evaluation comparing empirical distributions of tr(S), tr(S^2), tr(S^4), and tr(S^5) against ground truth in Figure 3. Existing data splits, training settings, sampling procedures, and benchmark distance metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Figure 3 examines how well generated SO(10) samples reproduce the shapes of four trace-statistic distributions, supplementing aggregate distance scores. The existing noise-scale and threshold sensitivity studies in Appendix E are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over five independent runs in the benchmark tables and retain the same mean/standard-deviation ablation plots. No run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-reporting changes are introduced.

E6.justification: Figure 3 adds empirical-density results showing closer agreement with ground truth for Niso+res than Iso+res on selected SO(10) statistics. Existing numerical results remain unchanged; for example, Table 2 retains Niso+res Reverse-SDE distance 4.60e-3 ± 8.24e-4.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.1 and 4.1, their proofs in Appendices A–B, the Tango-loss derivation in Appendix C.1, and the boundedness-assumption discussion in Appendix F.3 are unchanged. The new schematic restates existing mathematical relationships.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about score-function singularity, the two proposed methods, and improved generation on complex manifolds.

C2.justification: The explanations of scale imbalance, bias–variance tradeoffs, RSSM behavior, and rescaling remain unchanged. Sections 8 and Appendix F retain the same known-manifold requirement, Tango sampling limitations, computational tradeoffs, and future-work discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix D and Table 4 retain the same architectures, optimizer, hyperparameters, data-processing details, hardware, and dataset sizes. Sampling-time information and the code-access statement are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 49 references and substantive related-work discussions are retained, including positioning against manifold diffusion methods and prior normal-direction noise approaches.

P1.justification: Limited edits expand an author affiliation, correct 'Standard Bunny' to 'Stanford Bunny', change 'Experiment details' to 'Experimental details', and introduce the new figures. The overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v3 adds the method schematic as Figure 2 and the four-panel SO(10) density comparison as Figure 3. The alanine illustration moves and becomes Figure 4; the unchanged ablation figure becomes Figure 5. Equation spacing and figure/table placement also receive limited adjustments.

improvement.justification: The new schematic makes the existing score decomposition and two methods easier to understand. The SO(10) density plots supplement aggregate scores with directly inspectable distribution diagnostics. These provide modest gains in clarity and empirical support, while the methods, theory, main numerical results, and limitations remain unchanged.
